name: Measurement of the top quark mass: 171.77 ± 0.37 GeV

significance.note: A measurement, not a discovery; no significance is quoted.
significance.quote: The top quark mass is measured to be 171.77 $\pm$ 0.37 GeV.

summary.plain: CMS measured the mass of the top quark, which its paper calls the most massive fundamental particle, as 171.77 ± 0.37 GeV from 13 TeV collision data; the abstract says the approach significantly improves the precision over previous measurements.
summary.technical: 36.3 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV, lepton+jets tt̄ candidates, kinematic fit plus a profile likelihood over up to four observables: m_t = 171.77 ± 0.37 GeV.

title: Measurement of the top quark mass using a profile likelihood approach with the lepton+jets final states in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV
why_it_matters: The paper says that, because of its large Yukawa coupling, the top quark dominates the higher-order corrections to the Higgs boson mass and a precise top-quark mass sets strong constraints on the stability of the electroweak vacuum; precise measurements can also test the internal consistency of the Standard Model.
